AVTTSB.Title: Demon Lord Character Builder
AVTTSB.WrongSystem: The character builder works only in Shadow of the Demon Lord worlds.

Hint.ancestry: Choose your ancestry. It sets your starting attributes, characteristics, talents and languages.
Hint.attributes: Your starting scores come from your ancestry. You may adjust them once: raise one score by 1 by lowering another by 1.
Hint.paths: Choose a path for each tier your starting level reaches, and make the choices of each level up to it.
Hint.magic: Learn the spells your ancestry and paths allow. A spell's rank must be equal to or lower than your Power.
Hint.professions: You begin with two professions. Add the languages you know and mark the ones you can read or write.
Hint.background: Name your character and roll or write the details of their story.
Hint.equipment: Roll your wealth to find your lifestyle and starting equipment, then add what you carry.
Hint.review: Check the character and create it.

Restart.Title: Start Over
Restart.Content: Discard this build and start a new character?

Ancestry.None: No ancestries found. Ask your GM to enable a compendium with Shadow of the Demon Lord ancestries (for example the core book's), or to create ancestry items in the world.
Ancestry.Level4: You either learn one spell or gain {talent}.

Attributes.BonusHint: Your ancestry lets you choose an attribute to increase by 1.
Attributes.AdjustHint: Raise one score by 1 by lowering another score by 1.
Attributes.LaterHint: The "At your level" column includes the increases you choose on the Paths step.

Paths.None: No paths of this tier found in the enabled compendiums.
Paths.L4NoTraditions: Spells come from traditions you have discovered: discover one on the Magic step first, or take the talent.

Magic.Rules: When you discover a tradition, you also learn one of its rank 0 spells. Other spells must come from a tradition you have discovered, with a rank no higher than your Power. The counts follow your paths' instructions for the levels you gain.
Magic.L4Note: Your ancestry's level-4 spell is chosen on the Paths step.
Magic.NoSpells: No spells to learn: discover a tradition first, or no spell of your traditions is within your Power.
Magic.NoGrants: Your ancestry and paths grant no traditions or spells at these levels.
Magic.Over: You have more traditions or spells than these levels allow, or spells your traditions or Power don't allow (the level or a path changed). Remove some to continue.
Magic.FreeSpellHint: Choose the rank 0 spell you learn with this tradition.
Magic.FullTraditions: You can't discover more traditions: your paths at these levels allow no more (a spell you learned uses the same choice).
Magic.FullSpells: You can't learn more spells: your paths at these levels allow no more (a tradition you discovered uses the same choice).

Professions.Title: Professions
Professions.Rules: You begin with two professions. Your ancestry and paths may add more, or let you choose between a profession and a language; you can also trade a profession to speak another language.
Professions.Allowance: Professions {professions} of {maxProfessions} · professions and extra languages {used} of {budget}
Professions.Full: You can't add more professions: your ancestry and paths at this level allow no more (an extra language uses the same allowance).
Professions.Over: You have more professions or extra languages than your level allows (the level, ancestry or a path changed). Remove some to continue.

Languages.Title: Languages
Languages.Full: You can't add more languages: they share the allowance with your professions. Remove a profession to trade it for a language.

Background.Name: Name
Background.TablesHint: Choose an entry from your ancestry's tables, roll for it, or write your own. Some results give Insanity, Corruption or extra items: apply those on the sheet.

Equipment.LoadKitsHint: Reads the rulebook page set in the module settings; this can take a moment.
Equipment.KitsMissing: The starting equipment page wasn't found. Check the module setting.
Equipment.KitHint: Add the items you take (where the text offers a choice, pick one).
Equipment.LevelCoins: Higher level: roll 2d6 ss per level ({n})

Review.After: The system adds your ancestry and path talents when the character is created. Apply anything rolled on the background tables (Insanity, Corruption, extra coins) on the sheet.

Error.Name: The character needs a name.
Error.NoGM: A GM must be logged in to create your character (you don't have permission to create actors).
Error.Timeout: The GM's client didn't answer. Try again.
Error.NotAllowed: Your GM hasn't allowed players to create characters with the builder.
Error.TooMany: The build has more professions or languages than its level allows.
Error.TooMuchMagic: The build has more traditions or spells than its levels allow, or a tradition without its rank 0 spell.

StartLevel.Name: Starting level
StartLevel.Hint: The level new characters start at. The book assumes level 0; to start higher it suggests 1, 3 or 7.

PlayersChooseLevel.Name: Players choose the level
PlayersChooseLevel.Hint: Let players change the starting level in the builder. GMs can always change it.

PlayersMayCreate.Name: Players may create characters
PlayersMayCreate.Hint: Players without the "Create new actors" permission can still finish a build; the GM's client creates the character and gives them ownership. A GM must be logged in.

AssignCharacter.Name: Assign as the player's character
AssignCharacter.Hint: Set a new character as its player's assigned character when they don't have one yet.

EquipmentPage.Name: Starting equipment page
EquipmentPage.Hint: UUID of the journal page that lists starting equipment by lifestyle (the core book's by default). Leave empty to turn off.

LevelUp.Title: Level Up: {name}
LevelUp.After: The system adds the new levels' talents and enables their effects. Health, castings and other derived values update on the sheet.

Hint.paths: Make the choices of each level your character gains, and choose a new path when you reach level 1, 3 or 7.
Hint.professions: Add the professions or languages your new levels grant.
Hint.review: Check what your character gains and apply the level up.

Error.NotOwner: You can only level up a Shadow of the Demon Lord character you own, below level 10.
Error.Level: The new level must be higher than the current one.
